sweep_summary: Panará (pana1307) is in the catalog (fixed, right-edge: stress on the last lexical vowel, surface penult when the final vowel is epenthetic), deciding source = Lapierre's 2021 Amazônicas VIII handout. this search of works with stress in the title's single item, Lapierre 2023b IJAL 89(3) 'The Phonology of Panãra: A Prosodic Analysis', is the peer-reviewed statement of the same analysis and the best source for this language, but its body remains unobtainable by automated download (Chicago 403, closed per Unpaywall/OpenAlex, no the Internet Archive, no repository or author copy; web.archive.org itself unreachable). Its abstract, held from the prior check, CONFIRMS the classification verbatim ('culminative stress, which always falls on the last lexical vowel of a root or stem.. ultimate and penultimate stress, where the latter arises from.. vowel epenthesis'). Newly downloaded open texts : Lapierre 2023 Glossa 8(1) (p.6 fn.2: word-final [i] epenthesis + penultimate vowel lengthening, no rule), Lapierre 2024 LangSci chapter (transcription [ĩm.ˈpuː.ti] 'neck', no rule), Bardagil 2026 'Negation in Panará' (nothing on stress). No contradiction found; no reclassification warranted. Priority high for obtaining the IJAL 2023b body (and, secondarily, the 2026 J. Phonetics acoustic study, CC-BY-NC but bot-walled) to upgrade the strength of the evidence from grey-literature handout to peer-reviewed text.

new_statements.quote: Panãra exhibits culminative stress, which always falls on the last lexical vowel of a root or stem. This property gives rise to two stress patterns, namely ultimate and penultimate stress, where the latter arises from a process of vowel epenthesis that resolves a ban on word-final obstruent and approximant codas.
new_statements.citation: Lapierre, Myriam. 2023b. The Phonology of Panãra: A Prosodic Analysis. IJAL 89(3): 333-356. doi:10.1086/724988 — publisher abstract only (Semantic Scholar Graph API record held held by the project; article body paywalled, not opened)
new_statements.reading: First-hand author statement (peer-reviewed abstract): single culminative stress on the last underlying/lexical vowel of the root or stem = surface word-final stress, with surface penultimate stress exactly when the final vowel is epenthetic [i] after a root-final obstruent/approximant. Weight-insensitive (the CRV/CVC vs CV/CVː scale governs minimality only). This matches the catalog's deciding handout quote (§2.2 Stress) clause for clause; it is abstract-only and was already held as corroboration in the 2026-09-12 check, so nothing read this search of works with stress in the title changes the classification.6 fn.2; LangSci 2024 chapter; Bardagil 2026 negation chapter) states a stress rule.
